Ambrose Bierce, The Devil’s Dictionary.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/ambrose-bierce/the-devils-dictionary

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Ambrose Bierce, author, died about 1914 (Wikidata Q191050 gives 1914; Wikipedia gives 'circa 1914'). The death year does not change the result, see below.

First publication of the text used: October 1906, in New York: The Cynic's Word Book, first edition, New York: Doubleday, Page & Co. (Wikipedia, The Devil's Dictionary, bibliography). SE colophon: published in 1911 by Ambrose Bierce.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the first edition was published in New York in October 1906, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (United States): the country of first publication is the United States and the first edition appeared there before 1931, so the US rule settles the origin too, whatever Bierce's death year.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
